title: Was Babel Just Babylon? The Clues
author: QUILL
notes: Etemenanki link framed as hypothesis; Herodotus cited as description. Not-proven line in beat 10.

beats.text: Babel is just the Hebrew word for Babylon.
Two real towers fit the story. The strangest clue is a pun.
Babylon, in modern Iraq, had a great ziggurat: Etemenanki.
beats.say: Babylon, in modern Iraq, had a great ZIG-oo-rat: EH-teh-MEN-an-kee.

beats.text: Its name means 'house of the foundation of heaven and earth.'
beats.say: Its name means 'house of the foundation of heaven and earth.'
beats.label: ETEMENANKI

beats.text: Herodotus described a stepped tower of eight tiers there.
beats.say: Her-ODD-oh-tus described a stepped tower of eight tiers there.

beats.text: Today only its foundation survives, near the city of Hillah.
beats.say: Today only its foundation survives, near the city of HIL-lah.

beats.text: King Nebuchadnezzar II says in inscriptions that he rebuilt it.
beats.say: King NEB-uh-kud-NEZ-er the Second says in inscriptions that he rebuilt it.
beats.label: NEBUCHADNEZZAR II REBUILDS

beats.text: But a rival candidate stands at Borsippa, now called Birs Nimrud.
beats.say: But a rival candidate stands at bor-SIP-ah, now called BEERS nim-ROOD.

beats.text: The strangest clue: Genesis puns that Babel sounds like the Hebrew for 'confuse.'
Not proven: that either tower is the Tower of Babel.
Babylon's tower fell to dust, but its story did not.
Babel is just the Hebrew word for Babylon. Real ziggurat, or pure legend?

youtube.description:
Babylon had a giant ziggurat called Etemenanki, Herodotus described eight tiers, and Genesis hides a pun in the name.
Linking it to Genesis 11 is a hypothesis, not a proven fact.
